supporting_observations.claim: The alerted periodic HTTPS activity is attributable to C:\Program Files\CaseBinder\casebinderupd.exe, which was launched as Noah Kim's user process.

That process connected through the explicit proxy to update.casebinder.com, an approved CaseBinder update domain. The observed connections recur at roughly five-minute intervals from 13:39:30 through 14:09:02 UTC, consistent with the inventory's stated CaseBinder update-check behavior.

known_telemetry_limitations: DC-MAP-01 winsec logs were not collected from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC because of a collection outage. Other listed sensors, including proxy and Sysmon, were reported as operational.
The updater's proxy records show tunneled HTTPS connection metadata, not the contents of the exchange.
claims_not_established: The evidence does not establish the integrity or signature of the CaseBinder updater executable or the contents and legitimacy of the data exchanged in its HTTPS tunnels.
The evidence does not independently verify the remote server's identity beyond the proxy-recorded hostname.
unrelated_findings: Noah Kim's browser accessed a Google Docs document. Google Docs is not among the approved services, and the inventory prohibits other cloud-storage or file-sharing services; route for separate review, without using it to decide this alert. (T176-00085, T176-00086)

Kerberos activity from WS-NKIM-01 requested a ticket for greta.lund to FILE-MAP-01, followed by a FILE-MAP-01 network logon for greta.lund from WS-NKIM-01. This is outside the alerted outbound HTTPS activity and merits separate context review. (T176-00278, T176-00279, T176-00282)
